Task Satiation vs. Aggregate Jevons Rebound [M/S · unmetered]

Analytical synthesis separating micro-level task satiation — where extra tokens after a sound gate passes C(z)=1 add zero utility — from macro Jevons rebound when cheaper AI expands fleet power.

1/2 Intensive vs extensive margins:
- Closed-spec tasks (exact patch/proof check C(z)=1) stop profitably on first passing hit
- Under d ln E_total / d ln eta = epsilon_d - 1, cutting per-task joules raises aggregate kWh whenever demand elasticity epsilon_d > 1 (backfire)

2/2 Scope & open parameters:
- Synthesizes Jevons (1865), Khazzoom-Brookes, Nordhaus (1996) lighting series & IEA (~415 TWh -> ~945 TWh) datacenter projections [S]
- Long-run AI elasticity epsilon_d is unmeasured here; adversarial tasks do not satiate
- Unmetered (joules = null)
